haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. The rate-limit store is never touched, so no counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: Counters are per customer ID, so all keys share one budget: 100 per minute on Standard. Enterprise is undecided.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A denied request does not increment the counter and uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. An allowed request is already counted, and a backend 500 does not refund it.
haiku-low.q6: It fails open: the gateway forwards the request, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and sends no X-RateLimit headers. No retry.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is OPEN, meaning the limit is undecided by Product.
haiku-low.q8: In one shared replicated Redis, keyed rl:{customerId}:{floor(now/60)}. Counters expire after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q9: Each wall-clock one-minute window uses a new key, so the budget resets every minute. Old counters expire after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: A single atomic Redis Lua script reads the count, checks the limit, and increments in one step, so concurrent requests cannot overshoot.
haiku-low.q11: Retry-After is ceil(secondsLeftInWindow), where secondsLeftInWindow = 60 - (now mod 60), computed in the script. Minimum 1.
haiku-low.q12: No retry and no local fallback counter. The client gets the normal backend response with no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets a 401 Unauthorized. The rate-limit store is never touched, so no counter is affected.
sonnet.q2: Counters are per customer ID, so all keys share one budget: the plan limit total (Standard 100/min; Enterprise limit undecided).
sonnet.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
sonnet.q4: No. DENIED does not increment the counter, so a 429 uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. It was already counted when allowed, and a backend 500 does not refund it.
sonnet.q6: It fails open. The gateway forwards the request to the backend and emits the metric ratelimit_store_unavailable.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is undecided (OPEN); Product has not set the number.
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis (primary/replica), under key rl:{customerId}:{floor(now/60)}. The counter expires after 120 s.
sonnet.q9: The fixed one-minute window is aligned to the wall clock, so a new window key starts each minute with a fresh count. The old key expires after 120 s.
sonnet.q10: A single atomic Redis Lua script does the read, the limit check and the INCR in one step on the shared store. Concurrent requests on different instances therefore cannot overshoot.
sonnet.q11: ceil(secondsLeftInWindow), where secondsLeftInWindow = 60 - (now mod 60). It is computed in the script and is at least 1.
sonnet.q12: No. There is no retry and no local fallback counter. The client gets the normal backend response with no X-RateLimit-* headers.
